title: Per-tenant SLO decomposition and auto-suppress for long-tail alert noise
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: Teams were seeing alert storms from noisy long-tail tenant requests and false positives in per-route SLOs when a small subset of tenants generated sporadic token-heavy requests. This PR introduces a per-tenant SLO decomposition pipeline and an evidence-backed auto-suppression layer that dampens noisy alerts without hiding true regressions. Goals: 1) attribute latency and token-cost SLO violations to individual tenants and top contributing routes; 2) compute a sample-weighted anomaly score per tenant to distinguish systematic regressions from statistical noise; 3) provide a configurable auto-snooze/damping mechanism and an operator-facing SLO Lens dashboard to inspect suppression rationale. Changes included: - Telemetry pipeline: new per-tenant attribution keys (tenant_id, model_variant, route_signature) applied in the rollup job to produce tenant-level SLI rollups at 1m and 1h granularities. - Anomaly scorer: introduces a reservoir-weighted z-score computed from recent percentile deltas (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost deltas; scores are stored in the metrics-store as tenant_anomaly_score. - Auto-suppress policy: a stateful controller evaluates anomaly scores against configurable thresholds and historical persistence to either (a) auto-snooze alerts (with reason metadata) for short-lived spikes, or (b) apply a damping factor to alert firing probability when the signal is noisy but persistent. - SLO Lens dashboard: a compact UI panel (Console) that shows the decomposition waterfall, contributing routes, recent sample traces, and the suppression rationale with links to example traces. - Alert generator suggestion: when suppression is enabled, the system surfaces recommended dedup window and threshold bands per route/tenant to minimize pager noise. Implementation notes: - Rollup job: extended rollup-worker to emit tenant rollups and anomaly_score metrics; added a lightweight sketch-based reservoir to preserve rare-high-latency samples without exploding cardinality. - Controller: new controller service (slo-suppressor) runs as a low-throughput singleton per region and writes suppression decisions to the alerting-config store for evaluation by the alert router. - Backwards compat: existing per-route SLOs are untouched if tenant attribution is not present; suppression defaults to disabled. - Config: feature flag slo_decomp_autosuppress (off by default), per-tenant thresholds live in feature flags and can be adjusted via the Console. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for rollup and anomaly scorer (coverage added). - Integration test that simulates a tenant burst pattern and verifies suppression vs real regression behavior. - Load test: measured negligible overhead for rollup-worker (~1.6% CPU at 99th percentile on a stressed cluster). - Canary rollout plan: staged enabling on non-prod clusters, then opt-in beta customers, then gradual ramp with automatic revert if suppression masks >3 consecutive true regressions per week. Related work: references ENG-4829 for initial request, SUP-1937 for customer incident that motivated suppression heuristics, and dashboard design doc linked in Linear-ENG-4902. Risks and mitigations: suppression could hide real incidents if thresholds misconfigured — mitigated by conservative defaults, explicit evidence metadata (sample traces and contributing routes), and automatic rollback if we detect correlated increases in true-positive regression confirmations from alerts. Migration: no DB schema changes; metrics store adds new time-series keys (tenant_anomaly_score, tenant_sli_*). Rollout notes: feature flagged; requires console backend update and a single slo-suppressor replica per region. Checklist: - [x] Rollup emission and metric storage - [x] Anomaly scorer + unit tests - [x] Controller + integration tests - [x] Dashboard panel and links to traces - [x] Documentation (runbook + admin guide) - [x] Canary plan and automation

release_notes: Introduce per-tenant SLO decomposition rollups and tenant_anomaly_score metric
Add evidence-backed auto-suppression for alert noise with conservative defaults
Add SLO Lens dashboard panel showing contributing routes, sample traces, and suppression rationale
Feature flagged; disabled by default. Admin runbook included.
notes_for_ops: Enable slo_decomp_autosuppress flag to start collecting tenant rollups (no suppression until controller enabled).
Start with sensitivity: low and monitor suppressed_alert_checkpoint metric for false-suppression signals.
If suppression hides regressions, set controller mode to audit-only to collect evidence without muting alerts.
